title: Kingdom of Mysore
capsule: Mysore was a Hindu kingdom founded c. 1399 by the Wadiyar dynasty in the southern Deccan; by the 1572 attestation date it had broken free of Vijayanagara suzerainty following that empire's collapse at Talikota (1565). The kingdom was dominated for nearly four decades by Hyder Ali, a military commander who usurped effective power c. 1761 and his son Tipu Sultan (r. 1782–1799), who modernized the army with French assistance and fought four Anglo-Mysore Wars. Tipu Sultan's death at Seringapatam on 4 May 1799 during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War led to the restoration of the Wadiyar dynasty under British suzerainty, reducing Mysore to a princely state.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Tipu-era Mysore is well documented in both British and Mysorean records; earlier Wadiyar territorial extent before Hyder Ali is less precisely mapped.
